original_value: This study was conducted to test the effects of digital games on Asian students’ English vocabulary learning. Data used in this study were collected from Web of Science (WoS) and Education Resources Information Center (ERIC) from 2008 to 2018. A meta-analysis was performed to minimize heterogeneity between studies. The data were analyzed and visualized according to effect sizes. The results of this study showed that digital games played a significant role in promoting Asian students’ English vocabulary learning. This study also examined five factors that influenced students’ English vocabulary learning, including learning stage, game-aided teaching method, native language background, game platform, and game scenario. Effects of these factors were compared by referring to the standards for effect sizes. The result indicated that native language background had the most prominent impact, while negative transfer of native language hindered the vocabulary learning of Asian students. The effects of game platform, game-aided teaching method, and game scenario were not significant. The implication of this study is that creating context-based, high-quality educational games is a promising approach to promote Asian students’ English language learning.

result.paraphrase: This study examined how digital games affect Asian students’ English vocabulary learning. Its data came from Web of Science (WoS) and Education Resources Information Center (ERIC) for the period 2008 to 2018. A meta-analysis was used to reduce heterogeneity among studies, and the data were analyzed and visualized by effect size. The findings showed that digital games significantly promoted Asian students’ English vocabulary learning. The study also considered five factors affecting vocabulary learning: learning stage, game-aided teaching method, native language background, game platform, and game scenario. These factors were compared using effect-size standards. The results showed that native language background had the strongest effect, and negative transfer from the native language hindered Asian students’ vocabulary learning. By contrast, the effects of game platform, game-aided teaching method, and game scenario were not significant. The study suggests that developing context-based, high-quality educational games is a promising way to improve Asian students’ English language learning.
